paragraphs: Rabbi Yonah, Rabbi Mani’s father, was one of the mighty men of the Land of Israel. When the world needed rain, he would take a sack and tell his household: ‘I shall go and bring a zuz’s worth of grain.’ He would stand in a deep, secluded place, cover himself with sackcloth, pray for mercy, and rain would come: Taanit 23b. Rabbi Mani asked his father Rabbi Yonah. He was a partner with Rabbi Yose bar Chanina; see Rabbi Mani. Both were wise and pious, students of Rabbi Zeira, or Zeira in the alternative spelling Zeaira.
